newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds rally, new issuers jump into fray.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds rally, new issuers jump into fray.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds rallied along with Treasuries after a surprisingly weak U.S. September payrolls figure stoked U.S. debt and equity markets, dealers said.
Secondary trade was muted as dealers focused on the rush of new issues capitalizing on the drop in interest rates.
In the high-grade market, Travelers/Aetna priced $200 million of three-year A2/single-A notes at a spread of 25 basis points via lead-manager Smith Barney.
Dayton Hudson Corp issued $200 million in Baa1/BBB-plus rated five-year notes at a 54 basis point spread via lead-manager Goldman Sachs & Co Inc.
Norwest Corp set $200 million in AA3/AA-minus rated 10-year senior notes at a 40 basis point spread via UBS Securities.
Also, International Lease Finance tapped the market for $100 million in A1/A-plus rated five-year notes at a 37.5 basis point spread via Salomon Brothers Inc.
In high-yields, a "recession hint" in the payrolls report, which reported 40,000 jobs lost in September versus an expected 166,000 gain, capped the upside, dealers said.
However, a few junk bond issues did price. Mettler Toledo's $135 million in B1/single-B rated 10-year senior subordinated notes priced at par to yield 9.75 percent.
The bonds traded up to 102-1/4 by the close, dealers said.
All-American priced $100 million in B3/B-minus senior subordinated notes at par to yield 10-7/8 percent, sources said. The paper traded up to a 101-3/8 bid by the close.
